requirements.summary: logrotate.d/inventory-app config written with 'daily' directive, confirmed via cat and logrotate -d dry-run parsing 'rotating pattern: ... after 1 days'.

Config specifies 'rotate 7' and 'compress'; two forced rotations produced app.log.1.gz and app.log.2.gz confirming compression works and rotation count is honored (7 as configured); dry-run explicitly confirms '(7 rotations)'.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate mechanism configured; forced rotations show app.log inode (894710) unchanged across rotations, and writes made immediately after each rotation landed correctly in the live file both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (6aa805ba...) and healthy state captured, systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection loss observed during reboot, post-restart boot_id (79f223b0...) differs and matches the fixed after-executor snapshot, config/log data/timer verified intact, and rotation re-tested successfully post-restart.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, and continued application writability post-rotation via copytruncate — are directly demonstrated with functional forced-rotation evidence, not just configuration inspection. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently executed with a genuine boot_id change and full pre/post recovery verification, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is very good with only a trivial leftover state file in /tmp from test rotations.
limitations: No live application process was found writing to app.log at task time, so 'continued writing' was demonstrated via manual test writes (echo/tee) rather than an observed real application resuming writes; this is a reasonable proxy given no writer process exists.

Rotation count of exactly 7 retained rotations was not exhaustively verified by forcing 8 rotations; retention relies on the correctness of the 'rotate 7' directive as parsed by logrotate rather than an end-to-end 8th-rotation pruning test.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task: writing the logrotate config (cmd-6947241fdf924a55) is the core deliverable; forced rotations and test writes in the same command and in cmd-2a02449f73ab4953 are bounded functional verification of rotation/copytruncate behavior; the pre-restart marker write (cmd-ef9bb820f9674f31) and reboot itself are required by the mandated restart-evidence protocol. One minor residue: the --state /tmp/logrotate-inventory.state flag used during forced rotations leaves a leftover file /tmp/logrotate-inventory.state visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot (absent after-prepare). This is a small, low-risk artifact from test rotations, does not touch production logrotate state (/var/lib/logrotate/logrotate.status), and poses no security or functional risk.
